text:
Marisa: Quick sync — we need to land ownership and an ingestion contract for the new per-model/route latency + throughput panels. P50/P95/P99, TTFT, and tokens/sec are the core metrics. Who wants to own the runtime-side instrumentation?
Aj: I can take the ingest schema work if we agree on labels and cardinality. Question: do we want metrics keyed by (route, model_version) or (route, model_family)? Both?
Marisa: Prefer (route, model_version) for accuracy, but accept aggregated (route, model_family) panels for console perf views. Ownership split: runtime team emits low-cardinality rollup + high-cardinality detailed streams.
Todd: Runtime note — we already propagate `model_id` and `route` in request metadata, but not always `model_variant` or `quantization`. We need consistent tag names. Proposed labels: `route`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `quant`, `host_region`.
Sophia: From quota/cost side we need `tokens_in` and `tokens_out` per route too. tokens/sec should be computed both as sampling (1s) and a 1m rolling average for dashboards. Also TTFT = time-to-first-token (ms) measured at the runtime boundary.
Kai: UX constraints: console needs both a per-model summary card (single-number P95, TTFT, tokens/sec) and an expandable per-route timeseries. Also a canary view to compare old vs new model during rollout.
Aj: Proposed metric names (please bikeshed):
```
latency_p50_ms
latency_p95_ms
latency_p99_ms
ttft_ms
tokens_per_sec
tokens_in_total
tokens_out_total
```
All emitted with labels: `route`, `model_id`, `model_version`, `env`, `region`.
Todd: Implementing high-cardinality p99 histograms in runtime is expensive. Suggest runtime emits summary timers (p50/p95/p99) per 10s bucket and a lightweight histogram for sampling. We can also expose raw KV-cache hits/misses as `kv_hit_ratio`.
Marisa: Good call. For SLO alerting we want consistent buckets: 10s export at high-cardinality to metrics-ingest + 1m rollups at low-card. Ownership: runtime -> emit, infra/ingest -> validate schema & retention, eng-platform -> dashboard panels & alert recipes, console-ux -> visuals.
Sophia: For quotas we need a mapping: metric -> quota enforcement points. Example: tokens_per_sec used by rate limiter and prints to `quota.tokens_rate` gauge. Can runtime emit both `tokens_per_sec` and `quota.tokens_rate`?
Todd: Yes, runtime can emit both but prefer a single source of truth. Maybe runtime emits `tokens_per_sec` and quota service mirrors as `quota.tokens_rate` derived in ingest for clarity.
Aj: One more API debate: should we implement a dedicated /metrics/expose endpoint that returns the pre-aggregated series (for infra ingest) or push via statsd/prom-like pipeline? Both have tradeoffs. I lean push (prom gateway) for durability.
Kai: Console needs a stable query surface. If we change metric names later it's painful. Let's freeze names for 3 months after rollout. Also add an explicit `metric_schema_version` label for migration.
Marisa: Action items:
- Todd: add `model_variant` and `quant` tags in runtime by EOD Thu (owner: Todd). (1969123600)
- Aj: draft metrics schema JSON + retention/rollup rules and send to #eng-platform by Mon. (owner: Aj)
- Sophia: map quota hooks to metric names and confirm enforcement points. (owner: Sophia)
- Kai: mockups for per-model card + canary comparison by next Wed. (owner: Kai)
Can we also decide sampling policy? I propose full-rate p50/p95 and sampled p99 (1:10) on very high throughput routes to control cardinality.
Todd: 1:10 for p99 sampling seems reasonable. We'll add sampling config keyed by `route` in runtime conf.
deploy-bot: deploy status: runtime branch `metric-tags` merged to staging at 1969123705.
Marisa: Great, re-check on Monday after Aj's schema. Thanks everyone :+1: :eyes:
